headline: Emirates Squeezes Profits on High Fuel Costs Following 68% First-Half Drop
summary: Emirates reported a 68% drop in first-half profit before tax to $1 billion, with President Tim Clark citing high fuel costs rather than weak demand as the primary earnings pressure.
why: Emirates is one of the world's largest long-haul international carriers, making its fuel expenditure and profit margins a key health indicator for the global aviation sector.

impacts.name: Emirates
impacts.why: Higher jet fuel expenses directly compress the airline's profitability margins.
